scenarios.name: Fed Continues Measured Easing Cycle
scenarios.description: The Federal Reserve continues gradual rate cuts through Q1 2026 given moderating CPI (2.95%) and a softening labor market, bringing the Fed Funds rate toward 3.25-3.50%. Treasury yields decline modestly as the curve normalizes. Housing starts recover from depressed levels on improved affordability.

impacts.explanation: Base case for Fed easing cycle continues
Front-end cuts pull yields lower; demand for duration rises
Mortgage rates ease, improving affordability from depressed base
Looser financial conditions support modest growth
Easing cycle reflects underlying labor market cooling

scenarios.reasoning: Base rate from post-2022 easing episodes shows Fed averages 25-50bps cuts when inflation approaches 3% and unemployment stabilizes. Current data is consistent with this pattern. Clashing forces: services inflation persistence vs. goods disinflation. Moderate confidence warranted.
tetlockCommandments: Strike the right balance between under- and overreacting to evidence
Look for the clashing causal forces at work in each problem

scenarios.name: Stagflationary Trade Shock
scenarios.description: Escalating trade tensions (tariff reimposition or new sanctions) raise import prices, reigniting inflation while slowing growth. Trade deficit widens then narrows. Fed pauses easing. Consumer-facing sectors weaken.

impacts.explanation: Tariff pass-through raises goods prices
Trade uncertainty and higher prices suppress activity
Tariffs reduce import volumes, narrowing deficit (less negative)
Fed pauses or reverses cuts on inflation reacceleration
Slowing growth lifts unemployment

scenarios.reasoning: Base rate for tariff-driven inflation shocks in modern era is ~15-20% given political rhetoric, but actual implementation is rarer. Clashing forces: political incentive for tariffs vs. economic disincentive. Apply moderate skepticism to headline rhetoric.
tetlockCommandments: Strike the right balance between under- and overreacting to evidence
Look for the errors behind your errors

scenarios.name: Soft Landing Achieved - Goldilocks Continuation
scenarios.description: Disinflation continues toward 2% target without recession. Consumer spending holds steady. Labor market stabilizes at full employment. Industrial production accelerates modestly. Markets rally on policy certainty.

impacts.explanation: Stable consumer + business investment drives above-trend growth
Holds near current rate as labor supply and demand balance
Disinflation continues as goods normalize and rents cool
Steady demand and easing financial conditions support output
Real income growth supports consumption
Term premium normalizes as recession fears fade

scenarios.reasoning: Recent soft landing precedents (1994-95, 2018-19) suggest ~25-30% probability conditional on current data. Clashing forces: services stickiness vs. goods disinflation. Confidence supported by declining inflation and stable labor market.
tetlockCommandments: Strike the right balance between inside and outside views
Strike the right balance between under- and overreacting to evidence

scenarios.name: Mild Recession Materializes
scenarios.description: Cumulative tightening effects and softening consumer lead to a mild recession in H1 2026. Unemployment rises to ~4.8%. Fed cuts more aggressively. Housing and capex defer. Inflation falls toward 2%.

impacts.explanation: Recession contracts output 1-2 quarters
Jobless rate rises by ~70bps in mild recession
Demand destruction accelerates disinflation
Fed cuts aggressively to support economy
Consumer pulls back on discretionary spending
Recession fears and tight credit suppress demand
Flight to safety and Fed cuts lower yields

scenarios.reasoning: Base rate for recession within 12 months when Sahm rule triggers is ~60%, but Sahm rule is currently not triggered. With yield curve normalizing and labor stable, recession probability for next 12 months is ~15%. Clashing forces: easing financial conditions vs. lag effects.
tetlockCommandments: Strike the right balance between under- and overreacting to evidence
Strive to distinguish as many degrees of doubt as the problem permits

scenarios.name: Geopolitical Risk Spike - Energy Shock
scenarios.description: Escalation in Middle East or Russia-Ukraine disrupts energy supply, lifting oil prices 20-30%. Inflation ticks up on energy. Fed delays easing. Growth slows but no recession. Consumer faces real income squeeze.

impacts.explanation: Energy pass-through lifts headline CPI
Real income squeeze and uncertainty dampen activity
Inflation uptick delays easing
Higher input costs constrain output
Energy import bill rises, widening deficit

scenarios.reasoning: Base rate for geopolitical energy shocks in any 12-month window is ~10-15%. Clashing forces: ongoing conflicts vs. diplomatic mediation efforts. Tail risk worth including given current tensions.
tetlockCommandments: Look for the clashing causal forces at work in each problem
Strive to distinguish as many degrees of doubt as the problem permits

scenarios.name: Fiscal Anxiety & Debt Market Stress
scenarios.description: Rising federal debt (now ~$39T trajectory) and deficit concerns push Treasury term premium higher. Long-end yields rise despite Fed cuts. Mortgage rates stay elevated. Fiscal sustainability concerns reemerge.

impacts.explanation: Term premium rises on supply concerns
Mortgage rates remain elevated, suppressing demand
Higher long rates weigh on interest-sensitive sectors
Fed cuts more as growth softens
Deficits continue widening debt stock

scenarios.reasoning: Base rate for fiscal-driven yield spikes has increased post-2023 with rising debt/GDP. Recent term premium reemergence suggests ~15% probability of meaningful fiscal-driven yield dislocation. Clashing forces: foreign demand for Treasuries vs. domestic supply.
tetlockCommandments: Look for the clashing causal forces at work in each problem
Strike the right balance between under- and overreacting to evidence

methodology: Applied Tetlock's superforecasting methodology: (1) Established base rates from historical episodes (post-tightening cycles, soft landings, geopolitical shocks); (2) Decomposed forecast into 6 distinct scenarios spanning monetary, fiscal, geopolitical, and domestic dimensions; (3) Assigned probabilities reflecting clashing causal forces and balanced against inside/outside views; (4) Performed granular analysis of each indicator's sensitivity to each scenario; (5) Computed probability-weighted forecasts using linear combination; (6) Expressed confidence levels reflecting residual uncertainty after scenario decomposition; (7) Applied cognitive debiasing against recency bias on tariff rhetoric and overconfidence in soft landing; (8) Used continuous updating framework given evolving data through Sept 2026.
geopoliticalSummary: Multiple active geopolitical risk vectors persist into late 2026: (1) Ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict with periodic escalation risk and energy market implications; (2) Middle East tensions with potential for energy supply disruptions given ongoing conflicts affecting oil transit routes; (3) US-China strategic competition intensifying across technology, military, and trade domains with periodic escalations; (4) North Korea tensions and Indo-Pacific security concerns. Diplomatic mediation efforts continue but progress is uneven. These factors create tail risks for energy prices and supply chain disruptions that could affect US growth and inflation.
geoeconomicSummary: The global trade landscape reflects fragmentation trends: (1) Reshoring/friendshoring of supply chains continues but at modest pace; (2) Trade policy uncertainty elevated with periodic tariff threats and negotiations; (3) Dollar dynamics: relatively strong dollar supports import affordability but pressures export competitiveness; (4) Goods trade deficit at -$88.6B shows modest improvement (+24.4% change toward less negative); (5) Global disinflation largely intact outside services; (6) Industrial production recovering modestly post-2024 manufacturing downturn. Major economies (EU, Japan, China) facing their own growth challenges limiting US export demand.
currentEventsSummary: Key current economic developments shaping the forecast: (1) Labor market stable at 4.1% unemployment with payroll growth modest (+0.1%), suggesting cooling but not cracking; (2) CPI at 2.95% showing progress toward 2% target but services stickiness persists; (3) Fed Funds at 3.63% with market pricing for measured easing cycle; (4) 10-year yield at 4.77% with term premium concerns emerging on rising federal debt; (5) Housing starts collapsed -12.44% to 1.239M reflecting affordability stress; (6) Retail sales dipped -0.58% suggesting consumer caution; (7) Industrial production steady at 102.99 with modest +0.2% gain; (8) Federal debt growth (+1.43%) continues trajectory toward $40T milestone, raising sustainability concerns. The data suggests late-cycle dynamics with policy actively navigating toward soft landing while fiscal and geopolitical risks warrant attention.
